desc.concept: mid-sentence punctuation and small function words
desc.note: Windows show scattered positions at commas, 'are/be/was', and 'of/at/by' with no shared feature.

desc.concept: a single punctuation or operator symbol at a boundary
desc.note: Windows span math, code, and prose; the shared feature is only a bracketed symbol at a mid-text boundary, so evidence is weak and varied.

desc.concept: comma after a clause-leading phrase
desc.note: The windows share only a comma in varied positions; the comma token is the one consistent element, with no stable topic or structure.

desc.concept: commas and brackets splitting mid-sentence clauses
desc.note: Windows are highly varied across domains; the highlighted token is usually a comma or a fragment of a word, with no consistent feature.

desc.concept: comma or colon at a clause boundary
desc.note: Windows mix commas, colons, and other punctuation; the shared pattern is a punctuation mark at a split point, not one stable symbol.

desc.concept: commas and line breaks after clauses and names
desc.note: Activations sit on punctuation and whitespace tokens across unrelated texts, so the feature is weak and broad rather than a specific topic.

desc.concept: single-token insertion points across varied web text
desc.note: Windows are unrelated across domains (medical, blog, code, legal, French, Danish, Japanese), with the marked token varying each time, so no stable feature is evident.

desc.concept: commas placed mid-sentence before a following clause or list item
desc.note: Windows share a punctuation position but the comma sits in varied contexts (legal text, code, prose), so the pattern is broad and mixed.

desc.concept: commas and semicolons inside citations and numeric lists
desc.note: Windows mostly show a comma or semicolon placed mid-sentence, sometimes inside a number or citation, so the feature is a punctuation token in varied contexts rather than one topic.

desc.concept: mixed punctuation and word-boundary positions, no shared feature
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (medicine, code, news, scheduling) with the highlighted position varying from commas to spaces to word fragments; no stable feature is visible.

desc.concept: text fragments ending right before a comma or word break
desc.note: The windows are unrelated across domains (medicine, legal, sewing, coding, dialogue); the only shared trait is a bracketed token boundary, with no stable feature.

desc.concept: the copula "is" after a subject
desc.note: Windows mostly show "is" as a linking verb after a noun phrase, but the bracketed token varies in context ("is", "to", "Big", "lac"), so the pattern is broad and mixed.

desc.concept: is/in/to as mid-sentence connector words
desc.note: Activation falls on a variety of short function words and punctuation (is, in, to, MC, [[ ]] brackets), with no single consistent token across the windows.

desc.concept: Bracketed token at varied word or punctuation positions
desc.note: Windows are mostly unrelated topics; the only shared element is a marked position, so no stable feature is supported.

desc.concept: the copula "is" after a subject noun
desc.note: The highlighted token varies widely (is, over, on, from, into, by, men's, Person, part), so the recurring pattern is the position after a subject or noun phrase, not a single lexical item; "is" appears most often.

desc.concept: mid-sentence word or token completion in varied prose
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (politics, cycling, legal, math, web code) with no shared lexical item or format; the highlighted positions vary (setting, event, N, 0, dr, not, ave, a), so no stable feature is supported.

desc.concept: the word 'is' before a predicate
desc.note: Windows show 'is' after varied subjects; the marked token is a common copula, so the feature is broad and weakly focused.

desc.concept: the copula "is" after a subject, mid-sentence
desc.note: Windows are varied in topic; the recurring element is the highlighted token "is" (or "is"-like token) in a predicate position, but it is common and not strongly specific.

desc.concept: Marked token inside diverse text, mostly 'is' or 'for'
desc.note: Windows are unrelated across topics and the marked tokens vary (is, for, ObjectType, repository); no stable feature is visible.

desc.concept: bracketed token inside varied web and technical text
desc.note: Windows are unrelated; the marked token varies (is, Return, Tax, Gent, people, under, survey) with no shared symbol, word, topic, or format.

desc.concept: mid-sentence words preceding a clause boundary
desc.note: Windows share no stable lexical, topical, or formatting pattern; the marked tokens vary widely across unrelated text.

desc.concept: the word "is" as a copula
desc.note: Windows mostly show "is" in a copula or predicate position across unrelated subjects; the link is only a shared word, so the feature is weak.

desc.concept: the copula "is" after a subject noun phrase
desc.note: Activations sit on varied words (is, Jones, Nation, FA, the, art, of, see), so the shared pattern is mostly a mid-sentence verb or determiner slot rather than one clean feature.

desc.concept: token just before a double-bracketed masked position
desc.note: The bracketed spot falls on varied tokens (ene, is, and, be, findings) across unrelated text, so the windows show no single symbol or word.

desc.concept: Scattered single-token digits and short function words
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (medicine, aviation law, software, music, French health, birthdays) with no shared token or topic; the active token varies from digits to 'is' to 'or', so no stable feature is supported.
